title: The hornmad Iago ceaselessly willing that the moor in him shall suffer
html_source:
Horn-mad is found in Much Ado About Nothing Act I, Scene 1 where Benedick tells Claudio that he (Benedick) will never marry. Claudio responds:

“If this should ever happen, thou wouldst be horn-mad.”

In Othello, the villain Iago schemes against Othello.

Stephen suggests that this dynamic is an expression of Shakespeare’s inner conflict and self-loathing.
